name: Konstantin Nikolaev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Konstantin Nikolaev and his partners Nikita Mishin andAndrei Filatov formerly owned a third of Globaltrans, Russia's biggest private rail transport operator.
The trio sold their stakes in Global Ports, exiting the port business in December 2017.
He and his partners worked together at Petra, a railroad freight company.
forbes_facts: Nikolaev is one of the co-founders of Moscow management school Skolkovo, the first business school in Russia.
In 1996 the partners agreed with one of Petra's clients, Alexei Mordashov's Severstal, to start a transport company. They later bought him out.

name: Sergey Kasyanenko
forbes_bio: Sergey Kasyanenko cofounded Orimi, Russia's largest producer of tea and roasted coffee.
Orimi was founded in 1994 as the Orimi Trade company, which ran wholesale trade of flour, sugar and tea.
The company would become a major player in the Russian tea market, eventually launching its own tea packaging production.
Most of his fortune is cash, thanks to $1.5 billion of Orimi dividends paid over more than a decade.
forbes_facts: Kasyanenko has Ph.D. in Physics and Mathematics.

name: James Cameron
forbes_bio: James Cameron has directed three of the four highest-grossing movies of all time in 'Titanic,' 'Avatar' and 'Avatar: The Way of Water.' In total, his films have grossed almost $9 billion at the global box office.
Cameron's big break came with 1984's 'The Terminator,' a script he sold for $1 with the promise that he'd be allowed to direct.
At the 1998 Academy Awards, Cameron won Best Director, Best Editing and Best Picture for 'Titanic,' quoting his own movie from the stage: "I'm the king of the world!"

On the production of 'Avatar,' Cameron developed--often at his own expense--new film technology such as a 3D camera system, head rigs for facial capture technology and a simulcam system that allowed him to see his actors rendered in digital environments in real time.
When 'Avatar' earned nearly $3 billion at the box office, and millions more in DVD sales and streaming, Cameron earned an estimated $350 million before taxes and fees.
Cameron is also a renowned deep sea adventurer, making several dives to the real life Titanic crash site and becoming the first solo expeditioner to travel to the lowest point of the Mariana Trench.
forbes_facts: Dozens of UK celebrities, including David Beckham, Sacha Baron Cohen, Peter Gabriel and Guy Ritchie, collectively earned millions as investors in 'Avatar.'

name: Bart van Malderen
forbes_bio: Bart van Malderen is the founder and CEO of Drylock Technologies, a maker of baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, and incontinence diapers.
Drylock Technologies produces a billion diapers per month from nine factories, and had revenue of 1.2 billion euros in 2022.
Van Malderen has spent a career in diapers and other consumer products, working for 30 years at Belgian diaper producer Ontex, the family business founded by his father in 1979.
Van Malderen sold Ontex in 2002 and left in 2007 with a non-compete agreement. He founded Drylock when the agreement ended in 2012 to sell ultra-thin, cellulose-free diapers.
He is also the biggest shareholder of German diaper webshop Lillydoo.
forbes_facts: Drylock Technologies launched the world's first compostable diaper in February 2024.

name: Kutayba Alghanim
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2006-2020); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Kutayba Alghanim is the chairman of Alghanim Industries, which his late father Yusuf founded in 1932. His son Omar served as CEO until Dec. 2019.
Alghanim sells GM and Ford cars in Kuwait, owns a consumer electronics retailer and Wendys restaurants in the Middle East, among other businesses.
Kutayba and his brother Bassam have fought over the division of assets they inherited and have turned to a Swiss arbitration court to settle.
forbes_facts: After graduating from the University of California, Berkeley, Alghanim returned to Kuwait in 1970 and opened a store selling luxury furniture.
In 2003, he turned his family's former summer residence in Lebanon into an orphanage and named it after his parents.

name: Severin Hacker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020)
forbes_bio: Severin Hacker is the cofounder and chief technology officer of popular language-learning app Duolingo.
More than 100 million people take language, math and music lessons on Duolingo each month.
Hacker, who grew up in Switzerland, started the company in 2011 with Luis von Ahn, who was his computer science Ph.D. thesis advisor.
He and von Ahn took Duolingo public in 2021. It did nearly $750 million in revenue in 2024.

name: Daisuke Sasaki
forbes_bio: Former Google executive, Daisuke Sasaki, usually referred to as 'Dice', is the cofounder and CEO of software developer Freee.
Freee offers cloud-based accounting and HR software for small and medium businesses in Japan.
Sasaki started the company in 2012 with his friend Ryu Yokoji, a former Sony executive, who's now Freee's chief technology officer.
Freee's share price surged in 2020 as demand for cloud-based services rose amid the pandemic, which forced people to work from home.
forbes_facts: Sasaki hails from a family of beauticians and wanted to be in the beauty business until he discovered data science while in college.
